intro.text: Kaladin's name for one of the men sent to murder King Elhokar Kholin.

items.text: Cleft-chin was one of Graves's men. Late in 1173 he and another man, dressed as Kaladin's bridgemen, were posted at the door of the king's rooms in the Pinnacle on the day the king was to die. When Kaladin came looking for Elhokar, Cleft-chin recognized him as the bridgemen's leader and judged him no threat to the plan.

Kaladin knocked him to the floor, but as Kaladin was getting the drunken king out, Cleft-chin came after them and drove a knife into Elhokar's side. Kaladin killed him with a spear thrust to the stomach.

appearance.text: His chin had a cleft so deep that Kaladin imagined someone had hit him there with an axe when he was a baby.

personality.text: Wary and scornful, he would not admit to Kaladin that he served Graves and looked down on him as a former bridgeman. Set on the king's death, he tried again after Kaladin had beaten him once, with no regard for his own safety.
